## Connecting evidence with practical decisions

I am a research and evaluation leader with graduate training in quantitative psychology. My work centers on using thoughtful measurement, sound analysis, and clear communication to support community mental health services and the people who provide them.

I also mentor doctoral psychology interns in applied research and am developing approachable, interactive resources for learning statistics.

## Featured research

**Telemental health and remote work: An exploratory analysis of their dual impact on mental health professionals' experiences during COVID-19 stay-at-home orders** (2025)

This collaborative study examines mental health professionals' experiences during the transition to remote work and care, including implications for service delivery and workforce well-being.

[Read the publication](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11414-024-09925-z) · [Browse more research](research.qmd)

## Teaching resources in development

I am designing an introductory statistics learning collection with guided explanations, interactive demonstrations, and practice activities. The first topics include distributions, sampling variability, confidence intervals, and statistical inference. These materials are being developed and are not yet published as completed lessons.

[Explore the course pathway](courses/elementary-statistics/index.qmd) · [Teaching and mentorship](teaching.qmd)
